problem: End-to-end object-goal navigation models rely on discrete-time RNNs for temporal modeling, which limits performance and generalization in complex environments. Liquid neural networks (ODE-based and closed-form CfC) suffer from gradient vanishing on long-horizon navigation sequences.
motivation: Continuous-time liquid networks generalize better in dynamic environments, but their gradient vanishing on long sequences undermines training stability in long-horizon navigation. Fixing their memory mechanism could give end-to-end navigation policies better temporal modeling.
key_idea: Replace the RNN in end-to-end object-goal navigation with a memory-augmented closed-form continuous-time network (M-CfC) that reconstructs the internal memory mechanism to mitigate gradient vanishing.
insight: Per the abstract, reworking the internal memory of closed-form liquid networks improves long-horizon training stability and temporal modeling. It also reduces parameters and computation relative to standard LNNs. No ablations are available, since only the abstract was provided.
method: Liquid Neural Network integration: replaces the discrete-time RNN in an end-to-end object-goal navigation policy with a continuous-time liquid network.
